hook: Banks flag no records for *36%* of farmers
hook_b: Banks flag no records for *36%* of farmers
tldr: Banks have asked the Telangana government for guidelines to give crop loans to tenant farmers, citing no official way to verify leased land.

beats.what: Banks say there is no government-certified system or database on tenant cultivation, and the Bhu Bharati portal cannot record loan charges for tenants.
beats.why: Without verified records, banks say they cannot extend institutional credit to farmers working on leased land.
beats.care: A 2022 Rythu Swarajya Vedika survey put tenant farmers at 36% of cultivators, at least 22 lakh families.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Banks also want an awareness programme for bankers on recording loan charges on Bhu Bharati.

cards.q: What would help tenant farmers get loans fastest?

qs: How can leased land be recorded without hurting landowners?
How much crop loan reached tenants this season?

facts.t: Tenant farmers' private loans carried average interest as high as *24%* a year, a May survey found.
Each surveyed tenant farmer cultivated about *seven acres*, owned and leased.

viz.l: Tenant farmers among all cultivators (2022 survey)
viz.verdict: About 22 lakh families farm leased land

learn.t: Bhu Bharati = Telangana's online land records portal.

watch: Whether the government issues guidelines for banks to lend to tenant farmers.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Crop loans elude tenant farmers as banks flag land record gaps

fact: Tenant farmers are *36%* of Telangana's cultivators but lack loan records
twist: Private lenders charge them an average *24%* a year; family debt averages *Rs 2 lakh*.
